speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Patient
text: point. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but identifying the cause requires specific details. Can you tell me if your chest pain worsens when you take a deep breath or move, and have you noticed any blood in your vomit? REQUEST TEST: Lipase, Amylase; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: LIPASE: NORMAL READINGS, AMYLASE: NORMAL READINGS, ABDOMINAL_CT: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those results; since your lipase, amylase, and abdominal CT are normal, pancreatitis and a perforated viscus are unlikely. Given the combination of vomiting and chest pain that isn't explained by these tests, have your symptoms improved after eating, and do you have any history of gallstones or recent heavy alcohol use? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, D-Dimer.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: LIVER FUNCTION TESTS: NORMAL READINGS, D-DIMER: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those results; normal liver function and D-dimer make biliary obstruction and pulmonary embolism unlikely. Can you describe the exact location of your chest pain, and does it feel like pressure or a sharp stabbing sensation? REQUEST TEST: Troponin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your troponin is normal, acute heart attack is unlikely. Has the chest pain radiated to your jaw or left arm, and does it occur specifically when you exert yourself? REQUEST TEST: EKG.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal EKG and troponin, acute cardiac issues are ruled out. Has the chest pain worsened with movement or deep breathing, and do you have any history of recent trauma to your chest? REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer (confirmatory), Request Images: Chest_X-Ray, Chest_CT_Angio.

speaker: Measurement
